opening_message:
Ticket 1: Belinda Fuentes (employee ID E039) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E039.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Belinda Fuentes (E039) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write unless their role owns the system; Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is not permitted. Granting write as the maximum allowed.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E039 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training are limited to read on any system (never admin). Admin request exceeds the maximum, so grant read.
reason: The request is for admin on Payroll, which no note supports. However, the two notes conflict on Belinda Fuentes's (E039) employment type: the HR note says full-time Analyst (max write on Payroll, since Analyst does not own Payroll), while the Security note says contractor with basic security training (max read, never admin). Given the conflicting records, the only access level valid under both interpretations is read (contractors with basic training are limited to read; read is also at or below the full-time maximum). Granting read is the appropriately conservative decision.
